workstream.title: Frontend and Accessibility: Implement Sandwich Download Manager v0.1 for Windows

request.title: Implement Sandwich Download Manager v0.1 for Windows
request.problem:
IMPLEMENTATION REQUEST. Product scope is already decided and approved by the human product owner (sepehr-product-owner) on 2026-08-03 in decision records DEC-20260803-001 through DEC-20260803-005, recorded in workbook/09-decision-log.csv with the approved product brief at events/EVT-20260803-001-product-brief.md. Those decisions are final for v0.1 and must NOT be re-litigated, re-analysed, or deferred back for further product direction. The required outcome of this request is working, buildable, tested application source code in the application repository, not further planning documents, reviews, assessments, or decision briefs. A workstream that produces only planning artifacts has not satisfied this request.

APPROVED DECISIONS. (1) Initial platform is Windows; macOS and Linux are deferred until after the Windows v0.1 release is validated. (2) Scope is desktop-only; the earlier phrase 'all devices and all operating systems' is retired, and mobile and web are out of scope. (3) Architecture is a single shared Rust core using tokio and reqwest for the transfer engine and persistence, with a Tauri front end rendering in the operating system's native webview; three separately written native applications are rejected, and Electron is rejected on binary size and memory footprint. (4) The v0.1 MVP is bounded to exactly five capabilities, listed below. (5) The license is GPL-3.0; a LICENSE file containing the GPL-3.0 text must be present at the repository root.

REQUIRED v0.1 CAPABILITIES. (a) Accept a URL entered or pasted by the user and download it using segmented parallel connections via HTTP Range requests, reassembling the segments into one correct file. (b) Pause, resume, and cancel a download, surviving both application restart and network interruption, by persisting per-segment progress to disk; detect servers that do not honour Range and fall back to a single-stream download without failing. (c) Present a queue view showing each download's progress, transfer speed, and estimated time remaining. (d) Let the user choose a destination folder, organize completed files by file type, and offer open-file and reveal-in-folder actions; handle filename collisions and reject unsafe server-supplied filenames containing path traversal. (e) Watch the clipboard for copied URLs and offer to download them.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS FOR v0.1. Torrents; video capture from streaming sites; download scheduling; bandwidth throttling; browser extension and native messaging host, which are deliberately deferred to v0.2; macOS and Linux builds.

ENGINEERING EXPECTATIONS. Produce a real Rust workspace with Cargo.toml and a Tauri application that compiles. The download engine must be a separate library crate consumed by the UI so business rules live in one shared implementation. Include automated tests that exercise real runtime behaviour of the transfer engine, including segmented download, resume after simulated interruption, Range-unsupported fallback, and filename sanitisation; source-pattern assertions are not acceptable as behavioural evidence. Report the exact build and test commands executed and their results as evidence. Do not deploy to production, use production credentials, or perform destructive operations.
request.desiredOutcome: Hand off directly to engineering against the approved scope without reopening DEC-20260803-001 through DEC-20260803-005.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The repository contains a buildable Rust workspace with a separate download-engine library crate consumed by a Windows Tauri application, plus a root GPL-3.0 LICENSE.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run the documented clean build commands on Windows and inspect workspace dependencies and the root license file.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A URL can be downloaded through segmented HTTP Range transfers and reassembled into the correct file; servers that ignore Range fall back to a successful single-stream transfer.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run behavioral integration tests against controlled Range-supporting and Range-ignoring HTTP servers and compare resulting bytes with the source payload.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Pause, resume, cancel, application restart, and simulated network interruption preserve valid per-segment state without corrupting the completed file.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Interrupt real test transfers at deterministic points, restart the engine, resume, and verify terminal state and full-file integrity.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The queue shows progress, current transfer speed, and ETA for active downloads and exposes understandable paused, completed, cancelled, and failure states.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Exercise the Windows UI against controlled transfers and verify displayed values and state transitions, including keyboard and assistive-technology checks.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Users can choose a destination, organize completed files by type, open files, and reveal them in Windows Explorer; collisions are handled without unintended overwrite and unsafe server filenames cannot escape the destination.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run filesystem integration tests covering collision policy, reserved names, traversal sequences, open-file, and reveal-in-folder actions.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Clipboard URL detection offers a download without automatically starting one, while non-URL clipboard content is ignored.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run Windows UI tests with valid URLs, malformed URLs, and non-URL clipboard values, including dismissal behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Approved v0.1 decisions remain traceable to the human product owner and are not represented as user-research findings.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Compare implementation scope and product communications with DEC-20260803-001 through DEC-20260803-005 and the limitations section of the approved product brief.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A testable Windows build supports evaluation of all five approved capabilities without adding deferred features.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Use behavioral scenarios for segmented download, interruption recovery, queue information, destination/file actions, and clipboard URL offers; confirm excluded capabilities are absent from the study scope.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Post-build discovery recruits representative Windows users based on documented screening criteria and records participant count, method, tasks, observations, and limitations.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect consented research records and verify every synthesized finding traces to session evidence rather than owner assumptions.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Usability evidence distinguishes observed task outcomes from self-reported preferences and captures critical failures and trust concerns.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Review the synthesis for source-linked observations covering task completion, recovery comprehension, filename/destination confidence, and clipboard expectations.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Platform expansion or browser-integration recommendations are based on recorded v0.1 user evidence and remain subject to human product-owner approval.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect the subsequent decision record for evidence references, uncertainty, rationale, and attribution to sepehr-product-owner.
